userJob: Have the page move as one thing rather than as a collection of separately animated parts
problem: Motion is decided per element as each is built, so the page ends with four durations, three easings and two ideas about what movement means, and none of them was chosen.
worksWhen: The page has any movement at all, including a hover and a focus ring
avoidWhen: Never, though the whole system can be one duration and one easing and often should be
mechanism: Decide the system once: how many durations, which easing, and what movement is for on this page. Then every element takes from that set. A page with two durations, a short one for controls answering and a longer one for something arriving, has a motion system.
risks: A duration per element, which reads as several pages spliced together
Easing chosen for how it sounds rather than for what the movement is: a control answering is not the same event as a panel arriving
mobileRules: Movement tied to scroll is the first thing to cut at 375, where the scroll is a thumb and the frame budget is smaller
accessibilityRules: prefers-reduced-motion stops the work, not only the animation: the end state is reached immediately and nothing is left mid-transition
Nothing that carries meaning may depend on having seen the movement
genericnessNote: Fade-and-rise on scroll, 600ms, ease-out, on every section in turn is the default of every page builder there is.
